recipes.name: Authentic Cincinnati Chili
ingredients_raw: 1 quart water, or amount to cover

steps.text: Place ground beef in a large pan, cover with cold water, and bring to a boil, stirring and breaking up beef with a fork to a fine texture. Slowly boil until meat is thoroughly cooked, about 30 minutes.

Add onions, tomato sauce, vinegar, garlic, Worcestershire sauce, and chocolate. Stir in chili powder, salt, cumin, cinnamon, and cayenne pepper until well mixed. Add cloves, allspice berries, and bay leaf.
Bring to a boil, reduce heat to a simmer, and cook, stirring occasionally, for 3 hours. Add water if necessary to prevent chili from burning.

raw_recipe.headline: Authentic Cincinnati Chili
raw_recipe.description: Cincinnati chili is Ohio-style comfort food! This recipe will feed a crowd; serve over hot spaghetti or have it 4-Way with onions and Cheddar cheese.

video.description: Craving a taste of Cincinnati? In this video, Nicole shows you how to make authentic Skyline Chili right in your own kitchen. Learn how to achieve that signature thin texture and warm flavor profile using unique ingredients like unsweetened chocolate, cinnamon, and cloves.
video.name: How to Make Skyline Chili

review.reviewBody: This is the actual recipe from Skyline. It was printed in the Cincy Inquirer in the early 70s. I use ground turkey instead of beef and the flavor and texture are the same (my wife says my version is better!). May need to make a batch soon!

Been making this exact recipe for over 40 years. Regarding too much clove flavor - don’t crush them, use whole cloves and allspice. I put mine in cheesecloth or something similar along with bay leaf so it’s easy to remove at the end.

Went to college in Ohio, and there was a Gold Star Chili walking distance from campus, so I had to try....Pretty much followed the recipe, except due to previous shade given to the cloves, I only used 3, and also used 3/4 tsp of Allspice berries (more than 5)--both of which I powdered in my mortar/pestle...and did the overnight--that was a lot of grease I didn't need to eat. Subbed 1T Hershey's Special Dark Cocoa powder for the chocolate square, and a 6 oz tomato paste with an 8 oz tomato sauce instead of the pint of sauce, and it reduced nicely. Served over whole grain spaghetti, plenty of shredded cheese, onions and beans--a 5 way. Awesome. With leftovers.

This recipe was printed by Publix when they had the Aprons Recipes back in 2012. My family still loves it. The measurements are different (the meat was fried, not boiled) but the ingredients are exactly the same. I found in both cases I had to tweak the measurements to our taste using less Cumin and Vinegar, more "ground" Allspice and coco powder instead of the actual candy bar. I also use a bit more Cayenne Pepper because we like a little more kick. Every time I prepare spaghetti my kids specifically ask that I make this chili as the sauce. Now, it's a staple in my house.
Lovely recipe that tastes like home! If you can’t find whole allspice berries, substitute with one teaspoon ground allspice.

We loved this! I've made it twice so far. I used a 1/2 tsp ground cloves, 1/2 tsp allspice, and 2 Tbl cocoa powder. I boiled the ground beef in the morning then refrigerated it about 4 hrs then scraped the grease off the top. Although I love the idea of getting rid of the grease, I think I should leave a little on for flavor and to stick to the spaghetti better. It makes the house smell great as it cooks. The onions shouldn't be added in as you cook it. They should be served raw on top.
This is the REAL Cincinnati chili. Any recipe that starts out, "Brown the meal", is an imposter, and you should turn the page. The meal is always cooked in the water. Jim

This recipe seemed authentic to me, and our guests all gobbled it up! Definitely will save this to make again. I used ground allspice and cloves. I also used an immersion blender to grind the meat up after it had cooked. Highly recommend doing that for a smoother meat texture!

I eat only plants. I made this recipe with the following changes: Substitute the Beef with Impossible Beef - ounce for ounce (remember impossible beef is 12 oz, not 16oz, so 2 2/3 packages is necessary for 2lbs. Impossible boils better cooked first. Using a 1/4 of the onions, sautee the onion in a skillet with a tbsp of olive oil until fragrant. Then break apart the impossible meat into chunks and add into the skillet on medium heat until browned, continuing to break apart until it is a crumble. I like to go a little over just brown, but not burnt. Once done, I continue on with the original recipe as instructed.

I remove the ground beef after throughly cooked and boil my spaghetti in the broth, then return the meat, tomato sauce and spices back over to the broth, once the noodles are removed. It’s my favorite chili recipe
I will definitely make this again.......but with only half the amount of cloves called for. They were over powering,
DELICIOUS! I'm originally from Cincinnati and have had this several times! You forgot to mention Chili Dogs! YUMMY!!

This is almost exactly how I have made mine for almost 50 years.The only major change I make is to add strong beef broth instead of the water. I can never understand what good sense cooking with water makes.
will be making this again!
Have used the recipe for years!
It was so authentic to the Cincinnati Chili I've eaten in restaurants.
Definitely tastes like the real deal, will definitely make again soon!!!

This is a great recipe. It is the same I have been using for years. The only difference is that my recipe calls for cocoa powder instead of chocolate. For any who are concerned about the fat content, be aware that spices are fat soluble so if you want to take it out, do it before you add them in. I have also made this with lamb and it's fantastic!
This was YUMMY!! We didn’t have all spice berries, so we used 1/8 of a tsp of ground All spice. My boyfriend is from Cincinnati and said this does taste like the “real” thing!! Thanks for sharing !!
I used our bumper crop of tomatoes instead of sauce and sauteed the onions and garlic first, and then the beef before adding the rest.
